answer:
What proportion of studies in Experimental Economics were conducted in a lab setting?

Answer: 18/18 = 100%.

Operational definition used: a study counts as "lab" if online.o == 0 (not conducted online) AND subjects.o in {students, community} (in-person subject pools).

Data source: project='ee' in the study-data CSV (meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv), 18 unique original studies (ids ee.1–ee.18).

Results: online.o = 0 for all 18; subjects.o = students (17) / community (1); experiment_country.o present for all 18. No rows were excluded (drop=FALSE for all) and there were no missing values in any of the defining columns, so the count is unaffected.

Corroboration: the replication arms are also in-person and non-online (online.r=0 for all 18; subjects.r=students for all 18), consistent with the finding.

payload.hypothesis: 100% (18/18) of Experimental Economics studies were conducted in a lab (in-person, non-online) setting, defined as online.o==0 AND subjects.o in {students, community}.
payload.workflow: Filtered study-data CSV to project='ee' (18 unique original studies); applied lab definition online.o==0 AND subjects.o in {students,community}; confirmed no missing/excluded rows; corroborated with replication arms (online.r=0, subjects.r=students).
